scenario: [RLOW.14.7]: the order applies at every level, so a synthesized terminal is followed at once by the terminals it induces, before the next terminal at its own level. Rule `r` has one `after 5_s` clause whose body nests an `after 1_s` ([LTAC.6.2.2]); rule `next` follows it in source. The outer clause's follow-up `$r_after_0` induces the nested clause's follow-up `$r_after_0_0`, so the emitted sequence is `r`, `$r_after_0`, `$r_after_0_0`, then `next`. A compiler that lowers the nested clauses first, because their timer emits are the outer follow-up's actions, and pushes their terminals as it makes them, emits the inner follow-up ahead of the outer one that induced it. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `after_clause`, which takes what `nested_clauses` pushed off the build and hands it to `follow_up`, which pushes it back behind the clause's own terminal and group.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule r:
    Trig
->
    log info "r"
    after 5_s:
        log info "outer"
        after 1_s:
            log info "inner"

rule next:
    Trig
->
    log info "next"
